usa.title: United States
goals: Protect the economy, jobs, national security and affordability
Address climate risks within a politically divided federal policy environment
Seek reciprocal emissions action by China and developing countries
negotiating_constraints: The November 2025 brief describes withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and promotion of fossil fuel development
Do not place an undue economic burden on the US while developing-country emissions continue to grow
China must cut emissions for the US to consider action

eu.title: European Union
goals: Lead collective emissions reductions while protecting economies and security
Maintain credibility around the 55% net reduction pledge for 2030 versus 1990
Mobilize effective climate finance with international participation
negotiating_constraints: The EU will lead but cannot and will not move alone
Security, economic growth and cost of living constrain policy
Financial assistance should reach its intended climate use
opportunities: Cleaner air and clean energy jobs
climate_risks: Increasing damage without dramatic global emissions reductions

china.title: China
goals: Protect economic development and vital national interests
Limit climate risks and improve air quality
Use clean energy manufacturing leadership to support transition
negotiating_constraints: Developed nations should take responsibility for historic emissions
Any Chinese commitments should require significant US, EU and other developed-nation action
Do not use climate policy to constrain development, markets or national influence
climate_risks: Sea level rise, droughts and heat waves

india.title: India
goals: Raise living standards and overcome poverty
Secure developed-country support for clean energy and adaptation
Achieve climate benefits without sacrificing economic development
negotiating_constraints: An unfair mitigation burden on India is unacceptable
Clean energy action cannot come at the expense of development
Rich nations must take significant action proportionate to past emissions
opportunities: Electricity access and reduced fossil imports
climate_risks: Climate risks to development and well-being

other_developed.title: Other Developed Nations
goals: Protect economies, jobs and national interests while addressing climate change
Secure an effective international agreement with broad participation
Support clean energy, public health and energy security
negotiating_constraints: An agreement placing the greatest economic burden on this bloc is politically unacceptable
The US and developing nations must also make commitments
Fossil fuel revenue and jobs complicate transition
opportunities: Public health and energy security co-benefits
climate_risks: Rising sea levels and prolonged droughts

other_developing.title: Other Developing Nations
goals: Protect survival and pursue the 1.5C objective
Secure debt-free finance for adaptation and clean development
Protect forests while improving living standards
negotiating_constraints: Ambitious action requires strong wealthy-nation support
Developed nations should take responsibility for historic emissions
Funding must enable rather than prevent development
opportunities: Leapfrog fossil fuels with clean energy
Finance forest protection and reduce land degradation
climate_risks: Food insecurity, extreme heat and displacement

climate_alliance_proxy.title: US Climate Alliance (experimental whole-US proxy)
goals: Show continued American support for the Paris Agreement
Influence official parties toward ambitious action
Share clean technologies and manufacturing to reduce transition costs
negotiating_constraints: Official briefing grants no formal negotiating standing, only influence
Subnational actors cannot bind the federal government or the whole US region
opportunities: State and city clean energy policies
Broad coalitions of businesses and institutions

other_developing_rest.title: Other Developing Nations (excluding Brazil and Saudi Arabia)
goals: Protect survival and pursue the 1.5C objective
Secure debt-free finance for adaptation and clean development
Protect forests while improving living standards
negotiating_constraints: Ambitious action requires strong wealthy-nation support
Developed nations should take responsibility for historic emissions
Funding must enable rather than prevent development
opportunities: Leapfrog fossil fuels with clean energy
Finance forest protection and reduce land degradation
climate_risks: Food insecurity, extreme heat and displacement
other_developing_rest.note: In the eight-delegation world Brazil and Saudi Arabia negotiate separately; this team keeps the rest of the bloc.

brazil.title: Brazil
goals: Deliver a credible outcome as host of COP30 in Belém
End illegal deforestation in the Amazon by 2030 while supporting rural livelihoods
Secure international finance for standing forests and a just energy transition
negotiating_constraints: Developed nations must lead on emissions cuts and finance
Oil and gas expansion and agribusiness are major economic interests
Forest finance must respect national sovereignty over the Amazon
opportunities: Large-scale forest restoration and avoided deforestation
climate_risks: Floods and heat affecting cities and agriculture
brazil.note: No World Climate briefing exists for Brazil. Its members read the Other Developing Nations briefing, which covers Central and South America. The goals, constraints, opportunities and risks below are author-written summaries of public positions up to November 2025.

saudi_arabia.title: Saudi Arabia
goals: Protect oil export revenues and the role of hydrocarbons in the global economy
Diversify the economy under Vision 2030
Advance the Saudi Green Initiative's afforestation goals and a 2060 net-zero target
negotiating_constraints: Resist language that phases out fossil fuels; favour emissions-focused approaches such as carbon capture
Developed nations bear historic responsibility, so there is no obligation to contribute climate finance
The economic impact of climate policy on fossil fuel exporters must be addressed
opportunities: Very large solar and wind potential
Carbon capture and the circular carbon economy
saudi_arabia.note: No World Climate briefing exists for Saudi Arabia. Its members read the Other Developing Nations briefing, which covers most of the Middle East. The goals, constraints, opportunities and risks below are author-written summaries of public positions up to November 2025.
